title: Vehicle Height & Bridge Strikes
whatItIs: Know your vehicle's full travelling height, including trailer and load, before you set off. Low bridge signs show the headroom: if your vehicle is higher, don't go under.

keyFacts.text: Overall travelling height over 3 m? A height notice MUST be displayed in the cab where you can easily read it.

keyFacts: The notice shows the height in feet and inches (or in both feet and inches and metres).
Height can change when the fifth wheel is adjusted, or the trailer is loaded, unloaded or reloaded.
All bridges with less than 16 feet 6 inches (about 5 m) clearance are normally signed.

keyFacts.text: An overheight vehicle MUST NOT pass a mandatory height restriction sign (red roundel).

visual.caption: Low bridge signs: red roundel = legal limit, triangle = headroom warning

a.label: Red roundel (max height)
points: Mandatory: unlawful for an overheight vehicle to pass

b.label: Warning triangle (headroom)
points: Warns of the headroom under a bridge or structure
At arch bridges: maximum safe headroom

onTheTest.question: Your lorry's overall travelling height is 4.2 metres. What must be displayed in the cab?
options: Nothing, as long as you know the height
A notice showing the vehicle height that you can easily read
A copy of the operator licence
onTheTest.why: A vehicle with an overall travelling height over 3 m must display a height notice in the cab that the driver can easily read.

onTheTest.question: At an arch bridge, how do the road markings help drivers of high vehicles?
options: They show where to stop and wait
They guide them through the highest part of the arch
They mark a lane for cars only
They show the bridge's weight limit
onTheTest.why: The maximum safe headroom at an arch bridge is shown on the warning triangles. Road markings guide high vehicles through the highest part of the arch.

traps: Changed trailer or reloaded? Check the in-cab height marker shows the correct height for today.
Some older signs show feet and inches only: know your height in both units.
Plant with a boom arm: load it facing away from the direction of travel to limit bridge strike damage.
